MeEventEnvelope.description:
One frame of the `/me/events` fan-in stream: a named event and its small id payload.

Every other stream's frame is the same shape as its `GET`'s response model, named by
`sse_responses`. `/me/events` multiplexes many differently-shaped events onto one connection, so
there is no single response model to point at. This envelope documents the shape every frame
shares instead: the event's name, and a small object of the ids naming what changed — never the
changed data itself, which the client re-fetches.

The events: `attempt`, `practice.session_updated`, `practice.matched`, `practice.accepted`,
`cv.read`, `media.updated`, `station_import.updated`, `message.received`, `coverage`,
`community_reply`, `debrief`.

QueueStatus.description:

RatingRead.description: How a rubric rates a competency, for a screen that draws a rating control or reads a value.

ReadoutSitting.description: The sitting, as the head of the document states it.

ReferralAdminRead.description:
One referral, as the person settling it needs to see it.

Emails rather than ids: a uuid is not on a bank statement.

ReferralHistoryRead.description:
One redeemed referral, as the person who issued the code reads their own history.

ReferralOwedRead.description: What the whole settlement queue still owes, however many pages it spans.

ReindexReport.description: What a re-index did, so an admin can tell "ran" from "found nothing".

RelationSizeRead.description: One table with its indexes, and what a row of it costs.

RenameRubric.description: A rubric's new title (R-7): set once at creation, changed later from the builder header.

RenewContract.description: New contract dates, and whether a suspension should lift with them.

ReporterRead.description: One partner reporter, for the admin Access tab.

RescoreRequest.description:
Re-queue the marking. Left empty, under the policy the attempt was

ResultAcknowledgement.description: A candidate's confirmation that they have read their result.

ResultTotalsRead.description: One result's numbers: the station total out of its maximum, pass, and critical concerns.

ResultsIndexRow.description: One sitting's decision progress. `not_decided` is candidates with no decision yet.

RevenueByPlanRow.description:
One plan's contribution to a partner's acquired revenue.

ReviewFieldRead.description: One rating a reviewer may set, and the flat `field_values` path it is saved under.

ReviewFormRead.description: What an examiner or GP lead can rate on a slot, generated from the sitting's rubric.
ReviewFormRead.title: ReviewFormRead

RubricDraft.description: A structure being written, sent to be checked, previewed or given draft instructions.
RubricDraft.title: RubricDraft

What a draft structure comes to, whether or not it can be published yet.

When it is invalid, only `problems` is filled: nothing can be derived from
a structure that cannot be parsed.

RubricStartingPointRead.description: One thing a new rubric can start from: blank, a platform rubric or one of the org's own.

RubricStartingPointsRead.title: RubricStartingPointsRead

SamlConnectionRead.description: An organisation's SAML identity provider, and the two URLs to give it.
SamlConnectionRead.title: SamlConnectionRead

SaveDecision.description:
A decision to save as a draft.

`expected_revision` is the revision this screen last read, or 0 when it has
read nothing. A save that does not name the current one is refused with
`decision_revised` (409), so two administrators cannot overwrite each
other's draft.

`revision` is what the client last read.

Required, so a client that does not send it cannot overwrite blindly.
SaveGpLeadReview.title: SaveGpLeadReview

What an institution's IdP metadata says, and which attributes carry the address and name.

The attribute defaults are the claim URIs Entra sends. Text is stripped before it is
checked, so an `email_attribute` of only spaces is a 422. The optional name attributes
are not required, so a blank one is stored as empty and read as unset.

ScoringJobRead.description: One marking job as the queue holds it.
ScoringJobRead.title: ScoringJobRead

ScriptWriteRequest.description: How much of the script to write before it is checked.

SearchHit.description: One search match. `excerpt` defaults to empty; this backend always fills it in.
SearchHit.title: SearchHit

SeatMembership.description:
An add by an admin that may hand a new account a temporary password (the platform
console's seat route and an organisation's team invite).

Only for an address with no account yet, and only because the invitation email
cannot always be delivered. The person must change it at first sign-in. Ignored for
an address that already has an account: the console never resets anyone's password.

SessionFeedback.description:
What one participant leaves after a session, matching what the legacy form asked for.

`would_practice_again` is the one field the legacy form always required —
a session either felt worth repeating or it did not, and that answer is
what a good-match signal is built from. The star rating was always
optional there, which this keeps: someone declining to rate a partner is
not the same as having nothing to say about practising with them again.

SetAllowance.description:
How many new stations a session for this exam may hold: null when access is paid for.

`stations_sat` and `plan_limit` are the progress bar's numbers: distinct stations this person
has sat, and the plan's total (null when nothing caps it).

SetPlatformAdmin.description: Grant or revoke, spelled out rather than implied by which route was called.
SetPlatformAdmin.title: SetPlatformAdmin

SiteStatistics.description:
The counters the landing page's numbers band shows.

Marketing figures, not analytics: they are rounded down to a readable
number and they are cached, because the busiest page on the site should not
cost five aggregate queries per view.
SiteStatistics.title: SiteStatistics

SittingReadout.description: Everything the read-out says, in the order it says it.
SittingReadout.title: SittingReadout

SizeForecastRead.description: Where the size is heading, or why it cannot yet be said.

SlotBriefRead.description: A candidate's reading brief for one of their slots, during reading time and after.
SlotBriefRead.title: SlotBriefRead

SlotRagSummary.description:
What several reviewers of one slot agreed, or did not, in the rubric's own rating.

Per domain, every completed review's ratings in it combine as one
(`rubrics.scoring.combine_reviewers`: the majority, ties to the worse).
The overall is the worst domain: one weak domain is what a reader must see.
The name keeps `rag` until the web app reads the rubric's own rating fields.

SsoCallbackRequest.description:
The token the broker handed back, and the organisation it was for.

`state` (SEC-015) is the signed anti-forgery value the sign-in URL carried
and the OIDC provider echoed back on the redirect. It is optional on the
contract — Clerk's flow does not carry one — but required for a provider
that runs the code flow (Entra), which the callback enforces.

SsoConfigRead.description: The whole arrangement, for whoever administers it.
SsoConfigRead.title: SsoConfigRead

SsoLoginRequest.description:
Which organisation to start signing in to.

The slug comes from `GET /auth/sso/sign-in`, which a sign-in page already
called to learn whether this visitor's organisation signs in elsewhere.

SsoLoginResult.description:
Where to send the browser to sign in.

A URL rather than a server-side redirect: the frontend owns navigation
and the platform issues no cookies (ADR 0004).
SsoLoginResult.title: SsoLoginResult

SsoSession.description:
A platform session — what a login returns, minus the profile.

The frontend stores these and reads the person from `GET /me`, so the user
object is not duplicated into this slice's contract; `identity` owns its
shape and the broker's job ends at the tokens.

SsoSignIn.description:
What a sign-in page may show before anybody has proved anything.

Deliberately thin: served without a token, to anyone who asks. No
issuer, no bindings, no counts — those are configuration.
SsoSignIn.title: SsoSignIn

SsoStatusRead.description: Whether sign-in through the organisation's own accounts is connected, and nothing of how.
SsoStatusRead.title: SsoStatusRead

StaffMfaPolicy.description: Whether this organisation's staff must sign in with a second factor.
StaffMfaPolicy.title: StaffMfaPolicy

StartCheckout.description: Which plan to buy. A code, never a price: the plan row owns the price.
StartCheckout.title: StartCheckout

StartedAttempt.description:
What starting a set entry returns.

Deliberately this slice's own shape rather than `attempts`' response model.
They would look alike today and diverge the moment either contract moves,
and a client of one should not break because the other added a field.
StartedAttempt.title: StartedAttempt

StationImportList.description: This owner's most recent imports, newest first.

StationImportRead.description: One uploaded station document and how far its drafting has got.
StationImportRead.title: StationImportRead

StationPhotosResult.description:
The version as it now stands, and anything that did not make it.

A partial upload is a result rather than an error: the files that worked
are on the station, and the caller is told which ones were not.
StationPhotosResult.title: StationPhotosResult

StationProgressChange.description: What one of the two actions did, in numbers the toast can print.
StationProgressChange.title: StationProgressChange

StationProgressRead.description:
One station this person has sat, or holds in a practice set.

`attempts` counts the attempts that exist; `entry_attempts` is the sum of
the counters on their set entries, which is what the per-station limit is
enforced on and what "reset attempts" zeroes. The two agree until somebody
resets, and showing both is how the console explains the difference.

StationReview.description:
A platform station version's fact check and agent run, returned by stations and by media
production. Never part of what a trainee is served.
StationReview.title: StationReview

StationSubtype.description:
One kind of station an exam is written in, when an exam has more than one.

An author picks one before generating a station, and the generation
profile it names steers the prompt.
StationSubtype.title: StationSubtype

StreamTicket.description:
A short-lived credential for one `EventSource` connection.

`EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header; see `core.streams` for
why this exists rather than a cookie or a token in the query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

StripeEventRead.description:
One webhook delivery from the ledger, with the fields support reads
out of the payload rather than the whole document.
StripeEventRead.title: StripeEventRead

StructuredCv.description: The sections a CV is read into. A section with nothing in it is null.
StructuredCv.title: StructuredCv

SupervisorCircuitRow.description: One circuit this person is named on, with the sitting it belongs to.
SupervisorCircuitRow.title: SupervisorCircuitRow

SwitchWorkspace.description:
Which workspace to re-issue the token against. `None` means the person's own practice
— a real destination, not an absence.
SwitchWorkspace.title: SwitchWorkspace

ToolCall.description:
What the worker posts for one tool call.

`call_id` is the worker's own and is echoed nowhere; it is here because the
worker sends it and a rejected extra field would fail the call.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolResult.description:
What the model reads, and what the browser is shown.

`result` is spoken, so it is prose rather than data. `display` is passed to
the frontend unchanged on the data channel; the backend never composes a
route, because which screen a thing lives on is the frontend's business.
ToolResult.title: ToolResult

TrackingReference.description: What a partner puts in one link, and where that link points.
TrackingReference.title: TrackingReference

TraineePage.description: A roster page that also says how many people match, so the first load need not walk it all.
TraineePage.title: TraineePage

TraineeResultRead.description:
A candidate's own view of their result.

Deliberately narrower than the internal record: moderation notes and the
evidence snapshot stay internal.
TraineeResultRead.title: TraineeResultRead

TraineeStationResult.description: One station of a released result, as its candidate reads it (T-8).
TraineeStationResult.title: TraineeStationResult

TrendPoint.description: One attempt, in the order it was sat.
TrendPoint.title: TrendPoint

TrialCandidateRead.description:
One row of the trial-attempt picker (rubrics plan §8, R-6): just enough to choose it by.

Answered by `attempts.service_trial.trial_candidates` and returned by
`rubrics`' trial-candidates routes — shared here rather than owned by

TrialLimits.description: What the free trial allows, so a screen never hard-codes it.

TrialMarkRead.title: TrialMarkRead

TutorMemoryRead.description:
Everything the tutor holds about you, in the order it would speak it.

Exists so "what do you know about me" is answerable without reading a

TutorMemoryRead.title: TutorMemoryRead

UndeliveredMail.description: The newest abandoned emails, and whether older ones were left off.
UndeliveredMail.title: UndeliveredMail

UndeliveredMessage.description: An email the outbox gave up on after its last attempt, as the console lists it.

UpdateBrief.description: The one field a published version will accept a change to.
UpdateBrief.title: UpdateBrief

UpdateCohort.description:
Rename an intake, or say which academic year it belongs to. Fields left out
are unchanged.
UpdateCohort.title: UpdateCohort

UpdateExam.description: Everything but the code, which existing plans and ref ids depend on.
UpdateExam.title: UpdateExam

UpdateGroup.description: Rename a group. Membership does not change.
UpdateGroup.title: UpdateGroup

UpdateInvoice.description: What the console may change: the PO number while issued, and the status.
UpdateInvoice.title: UpdateInvoice

UpdateMe.description: What a person may change about themselves. Absent means "leave it".
UpdateMe.title: UpdateMe

UpdateOrgDetails.description:
What an org admin may change: the name and contact. Not the address or contract.

A contact sent as null is cleared; one left out is kept.
UpdateOrgDetails.title: UpdateOrgDetails

UpdateOrganization.description: What a platform administrator may change about an organisation. Not the slug.
UpdateOrganization.title: UpdateOrganization

UpdatePilotConfig.description:
Change a pilot's rate or its alerts. Fields left out are unchanged.

`reset_spend_alerts` forgets which thresholds have already alerted, so
raised or lowered thresholds are judged afresh.
UpdatePilotConfig.title: UpdatePilotConfig

UpdatePlan.description:
A staff change to a plan: take it on or off sale, and/or set how many stations it unlocks.

Leaving `station_limit` out of the request body means "do not change it"; sending it
explicitly as `null` means "no limit". The handler tells the two apart with
`"station_limit" in body.model_fields_set`, not by checking for `None`.
UpdatePlan.title: UpdatePlan

UpdateSet.description:
What a platform admin may change about one of their own sets (a learner may not: `forbidden`).

The name, and — since this replaces the legacy "edit session" screen — the
stations themselves. Swapping the list does not touch an entry that stays
in it: its counters are what an attempt points at, so `replace_entries`
matches kept versions back onto their existing entry rather than deleting
and recreating it. A set carries no description and no timings — the
length of a session is the sum of its stations' exam timings, which the
exam owns — so there is nothing else to write.

Whitespace strips to nothing, which is then too short: a set called `"   "`
is an unlabelled row in the list the learner has to keep.

`station_version_ids` left out (`None`) means "just the name"; an empty
list is a real request to empty the set, and is rejected only if that
would mean removing a station that already has an attempt against it.
UpdateSet.title: UpdateSet

UpdateSitting.description:
Fields to change on a sitting. An omitted field is left alone.

`status` is not offered here: that belongs to the run machine, not this
route.
UpdateSitting.title: UpdateSitting

UpdateStationFlag.description:
Closing a report, or reopening one.

One body for both because they are one decision — has this been dealt with?
— and a separate `reopen` route would be the same write with the flag
reversed.
UpdateStationFlag.title: UpdateStationFlag

UpdateTrainee.description:
Correct a trainee's name or intake. Fields left out are unchanged; a field sent
as null clears it. The email address cannot be changed here. Group membership is
set separately via `PUT /trainee-groups/{id}/members`.
UpdateTrainee.title: UpdateTrainee

UserSummary.description: An account as the console lists it. No password state, no memberships.
UserSummary.title: UserSummary

VoiceGrant.description:
What the browser needs to join a room with its patient or tutor. No agent
name or backend label: those are dispatch details the client has no use for.
VoiceGrant.title: VoiceGrant

VoiceQueueStanding.description:
A candidate's place in line while every voice seat is taken.

`position` is 1 at the front. `ready` means a seat is free for them now:
ask for the token again and it is theirs. Sent as the 202 body of the
token request and as each frame of the waiting stream.
VoiceQueueStanding.title: VoiceQueueStanding

WorkerBootstrap.description:
`{attempt, scenario}` — the only thing a worker is told.

Both halves are passed through as the engine's own documents rather than
re-modelled here: re-describing them would create a second definition of a
contract the engine already owns, free to drift.
WorkerBootstrap.title: WorkerBootstrap

WorkerSessionPayload.description:
`{"session": {...}}` — the shape `livekit_assistant_worker` validates.

Its paths are hardcoded in the worker rather than configured per backend, so
this API must mount them exactly. Noted in the README.
WorkerSessionPayload.title: WorkerSessionPayload

app__features__assistant__schemas__RoomG.description:
What the browser needs to join this session's room, and nothing more.

The same three fields `voice` returns for a circuit's room. Restated here
rather than imported because a router may name only its own slice's
schemas, and the response shape is this route's contract either way.

app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.description: Returned where the answer must not depend on whether a record exists.
app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.title: Accepted

app__features__media__schemas__MediaRead.description:
One piece of study material.

`content` is the paid body — the slide deck, the summary, the article. It
is `None` for a reader who does not hold the exam it belongs to, and
`locked` says which happened, so the client can show an upgrade prompt
rather than an empty page. Everything else — title, summary — is public.
app__features__media__schemas__MediaRead.title: MediaRead

app__features__media_production__schemas.description: Same fields as media's item read, owned here so this slice's contract stands alone.
app__features__media_production__schemas.title: MediaRead

app__features__peer_practice__schemas__R.description:
What a browser needs to join a peer session's room.

This slice's own shape rather than `voice`'s or `sittings`', for the
reason those two do not share one either: a wire contract belongs to the
routes that serve it.
app__features__peer_practice__schemas__R.title: RoomGrant

app__features__sittings__schemas__RoomGr.description:
What a browser needs to join a circuit's room, and nothing more.

A candidate taking their place before their station starts, or an examiner
stepping in to watch. Neither names a recording: the candidate has none
yet and the examiner never will.
app__features__sittings__schemas__RoomGr.title: RoomGrant

Rebuild the material index now, rather than waiting for tonight's run. Synchronous:
the response confirms the material is searchable.

get.description:
The demo scenarios a first-time user is walked through.

Answered from the same pack the onboarding session's instructions are
rendered from, and for the caller's own exam — a headache for SCA, chest
pain for PLAB — so the introduction is to the thing they are sitting.

post.description: The browser's way into an assistant session's room.

The candidate walks away before finishing.

Otherwise the attempt stays `running` forever, holding the slot's one live
attempt and counting as in progress on every screen that reads it.

get.description:
What the candidate reads before the patient is called.

Keyed on the attempt, not the station: the library's own read carries no
content on purpose, because browsing is open to everybody and the brief is
part of the exam. Having started the station is what makes it readable.

The attempt's marking as a feedback screen draws it: the rubric frozen on
the attempt, its resolved display, and each result with the totals that
rubric makes of it (total, maximum, pass, critical concerns, per domain).

A page rather than one result: re-scoring under a new policy adds beside
the old, so a candidate's history stays readable — to the same two people as
the transcript, which is `service_access.ensure_readable`.

The model answer: the patient's ideas and concerns, and the plan.

Refused until the consultation is over — before that it is the answer to
the station being sat.

The attempt, pushed until it is marked.

Marking is a background job taking a minute or two of model time, so the
page has to learn it finished. This replaces b2c's feedback-status
stream, its poller and the second poller behind that.

get.description: The candidate's own turns, and the examiner named on their circuit.

post.description: Sign in here with the session the old backend already gave you.
Ends the presented session, or every session when none is named.

Trade the broker's token for a platform session.

The browser is sent here by the frontend callback page with the token the
broker appended. The token is verified against the broker — never decoded
and trusted — and the person is provisioned on first sign-in, because the
institution vouches for them and there is no password to have lost.

Where to send the browser to sign in to this organisation.

Unauthenticated: this is the first step of signing in, before anybody
has. The URL is returned rather than followed — the frontend owns
navigation and the platform sets no cookies (ADR 0004).

Whether this visitor's organisation signs in somewhere else.

Unauthenticated, and it has to be: this is what a sign-in page asks
before anybody has signed in. `null` means "sign in here, with a
password", which is the ordinary case and what every host that is not a
partner's gets: a 200, not a 404, because it is not an error.
